intro: Professionals and everyday users convert horsepower (hp) (hp) to watts (W) when working across imperial and si standards in automotive engine output ratings, electric motor sizing, solar inverter specifications, and appliance load planning. One horsepower (mechanical) equals 745.699872 watts, while 1 watt equals 0.001341 horsepower (hp). Whether you are verifying power specifications on imported equipment, cross-checking technical datasheets, or scaling practical measurements, this converter applies the exact NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 reference relationship with instant precision.

mistakesAndEdgeCases.title: Exact NIST Factor vs. Early Rounding Drift
items: The exact conversion factor from Horsepower (Mechanical) to Watt is 745.69987158, derived from the 1959 International Yard and Pound Agreement (1 inch = 25.4 mm, 1 lb = 0.45359237 kg).

In structural engineering, CNC machining, or bulk inventory totals, rounding the multiplier to 2 decimal places too early can introduce cumulative tolerance errors; always compute with the full factor and round only the final displayed figure.

faqs.question: How many watts (W) are in 1 horsepower (mechanical) (hp)?
faqs.answer: There are 745.69987158 watts (W) in 1 horsepower (mechanical) (hp), which rounds to 745.6999 W for everyday calculations. Conversely, 1 watt equals 0.001341 horsepower (hp).

faqs.question: How do I convert horsepower (hp) to watts (hp to W)?
faqs.answer: To convert horsepower (hp) to watts, use the formula: W = hp × 745.69987158. For example, converting 2 hp gives 1,491.3997 W.

faqs.question: What is 2 horsepower (hp) in watts?
faqs.answer: 2 horsepower (hp) (hp) equals exactly 1,491.3997 watts (W) using standard NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 conversion factors.
